correctness.rationale: For odd primes, 4P on the Q-P linear solution factors as (y+1)^2(9y^2+4y+4). Hensel at p>=5 yields a separated double root and two possible simple roots. At p=3, the quadratic has a unique integral root of exact valuation 2 and a unit cofactor, permitting exact valuation-branch counts. At p=2, the difference congruence leaves exactly two x lifts for each y; the even/odd y valuation cases give the exact low-power and stable formulas. CRT proves arbitrary moduli. The existing theorem of Kabluchko–Marynych applies because the original polynomials are coprime. Local and global moment thresholds follow from the uniform p^{k/2} growth and Euler-factor estimates. The standalone checker passed 71 prime-power cases, 29 direct brute checks and 19 composite cases; these are checks, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: A complete natural finite-prime-power classification of the intersection multiplicities of two diagonal-translated cusp curves; a genuinely singular double-root branch causes p^{k/2} growth, and exact exceptional p=2 and p=3 laws are necessary to obtain the full Euler product. This gives a sharp new arithmetic contrast between each prime-local 3/2 moment boundary and the global 1 boundary. It is neither a finite experiment nor a bare restatement of generic convergence.
